title: SuwalkiMesh Router Troubleshooting and Status Lights
content:
Status Light Reference

The SuwalkiMesh router reports its state with a single light on the front panel.

Solid green

    The router has power and a working line. A problem at this point is usually with one device or with Wi-Fi coverage, not with the line.

Blinking or solid red

    The router has power but no signal from the network. Power-cycle the unit: unplug it, wait 30 seconds, plug it back in, and allow up to 3 minutes for the light to settle.

Amber

    The router is starting up or applying a firmware update. Do not unplug it. Amber for more than 10 minutes means the update failed.

No light at all

    The unit is not receiving power. Check both ends of the power cable and try a different wall socket before assuming a hardware fault.

Common Issues

Slow speed on one device only

    Almost always a device or coverage issue rather than a line fault. Test on a second device, and over a cable if one is available.

Wi-Fi drops in one room

    Typical of a coverage gap. Fiber 1500 ships with a second mesh unit; other plans can add one for $4/month.

Everything down after a storm

    Check for a reported outage before troubleshooting the router. A local outage cannot be resolved from the customer side.

Escalation

    A red light that survives two power cycles needs a technician

    An amber light stuck past 10 minutes needs a replacement unit

    Support phone: 800-555-0177
llm_guide:
**LLM Guide - SuwalkiMesh Router Troubleshooting**

**THE MOST IMPORTANT**
- Ask what colour the status light is before suggesting anything. The colour decides the whole path, and guessing wastes the customer time.
- This article backs the self-router-health-check procedure. While that procedure runs, follow its steps and use this article for detail.

**Topics to Cover**
1. What each light colour means: green, red, amber, no light.
2. The 30-second power cycle and the 3-minute settle time.
3. Telling a line fault from a single-device or coverage problem.
4. When to escalate to a technician or a replacement unit.

**Key Points to Emphasize**
- Green means the line is fine; look at the device or the Wi-Fi instead.
- Never tell a customer to unplug a router showing amber.
- Check for a known outage before a long troubleshooting sequence.

**Tone**
- Patient and step by step. One instruction at a time, then wait for the customer to report back.

HomeExpert Plus – $16.99/month

title: SuwalkiMesh Whole-Home Wi-Fi
content:
Overview

Every SuwalkiCable internet plan includes a SuwalkiMesh unit. The system pairs Wi-Fi 6 and Wi-Fi 7 hardware with the fiber line to remove dead spots across the home.

Wi-Fi 7 Capabilities

    Higher throughput and wider coverage than the previous generation

    Lower latency, which matters for gaming and video calls

    Multi-link operation keeps many devices responsive at once

    Built for households that keep adding connected devices

SuwalkiMesh Technologies

PathPick

    Routes traffic around congestion inside the home so one heavy device does not slow the rest.

HandOff

    Moves a device to the strongest unit as the user walks between rooms, without dropping the connection.

BandSelect

    Picks the least congested channel automatically instead of leaving it to a fixed setting.

Security

    WPA3 encryption on every unit

    Automatic firmware and security updates

    Household profiles and content filtering at no extra cost

Equipment by Plan

    Fiber 200 – one SuwalkiMesh W6 unit

    Fiber 600 – one SuwalkiMesh W7 unit

    Fiber 1500 – two SuwalkiMesh W7 units

    Additional units on any plan – $4/month each
